name: Project Work Plan
one_liner: What work, by whom, how much it costs and when it happens.
purpose: The Project Work Plan further elaborates the project scope and identifies and organises the work and deliverables needed to achieve the project goals. It establishes the basis for estimating duration, calculating resources and scheduling the work, and is then used to monitor progress and control the project. It is baselined and kept up to date for the life of the project.

fields.what: Elaborates the Charter's scope baseline to a finer level of detail, including deliverables and sub-deliverables. It must not introduce new or different scope.
fields.castor: Configurable lending platform giving straight-through processing from loan agreement to disbursement to repayment schedule.

fields.what: Every component has a type: Deliverable, Activity, Task or Work Package. Each lower level gives a finer view of the work.
fields.castor: Deliverable 1.3 Release 1 — product configuration engine; Activity 1.3.2 Configure instrument templates.

fields.what: The project itself is 1.0; second level 1.1, 1.2 …; third level 1.1.1, 1.1.2 …; fourth 1.1.1.1. IDs must match across all three parts.
fields.castor: 1.0 Project CASTOR · 1.3 Release 1 · 1.3.2 Configure instrument templates · 1.3.2.1 PCCL/ECCL template.

fields.what: A unique name per component, placed at the correct indent level of the five-column breakdown table.
fields.castor: 1.5 Parallel run with LOS; 1.6 Transition & go-live; 1.7 Business implementation.

fields.what: A short description per deliverable, activity and task; level of detail should match the audience and the component's importance.
fields.castor: 1.5 Parallel run: run CASTOR and LOS side by side on live disbursements and compare reconciliation output daily.

fields.what: Choose one representation: deliverables-based, work-based, by part of the organisation involved, or phase-based.
fields.castor: Deliverables-based, aligned to the two releases plus parallel run, transition and business implementation.

fields.what: Which components must complete before this one can start — the input to sequencing and to the overall duration.
fields.castor: 1.3 Release 1 depends on 1.2 contract award (18 Sep 2026); 1.6 transition depends on 1.5 parallel run.

fields.what: The resource or resource profile assigned to the component; assignment is what makes a cost calculable.
fields.castor: Levallois implementation team, ESM solution architect (Nikola Tesla), business analyst (Ada Lovelace).

fields.what: Estimated effort for the component, in the chosen unit — normally person-days — based on resource availability and capability.
fields.who: PM with task owners and experts
fields.castor: 3,100 PD in total: 820 PD on Release 1, 940 PD on Release 2, 360 PD on the parallel run.

fields.what: Cost of the component, derived from the quantity and the cost per unit for each assigned resource. Include internal and external resources.
fields.who: PM calculates · PO owns the budget
fields.castor: €8.4 m total; €2.4 m Release 1, €2.8 m Release 2, €0.6 m business implementation.

fields.what: State the method(s) used — expert advice, historical information, similarity to other tasks — and include contingency for known uncertainty.
fields.who: PM documents · PCT and experts input
fields.castor: Expert advice from Leonardo da Vinci' division plus vendor benchmarks; contingency held against risk R-07.

fields.what: List every resource the project needs, distinguishing human resources from non-human ones (software, hardware, equipment, facilities, supplies, materials).
fields.castor: In-house core team plus outsourced platform implementation (Mix delivery), test environments and a training room.

fields.what: Unique identifier per resource, human (H.n) or material (M.n), reused across the cost, availability and contingency tables.
fields.castor: H.1 solution architect · H.4 loan-operations SME · M.2 parallel-run test environment.

fields.what: The window during which the resource is needed by the project.
fields.castor: Levallois implementation team from 18 Sep 2026 to 30 Apr 2028; trainers from Jan 2028.

fields.f: Resource Plan — Skill and Skill level
fields.what: The skills the resource must have and the level required to guarantee the quality of the deliverables.
fields.castor: Platform configuration — advanced; ESM disbursement process knowledge — expert (Grace Hopper's team).

fields.what: For non-human resources, the properties that matter: capacity, version, specification, seats.
fields.castor: Parallel-run environment: full copy of live loan data, restricted access, 30-seat training room.

fields.what: How many units of the resource are needed (number of people, licences, rooms).
fields.castor: Two ESM business analysts, one solution architect, one dedicated test environment.

fields.what: Cost per unit × number of units = total cost, per resource. Another view of the costs already in section 3.1.
fields.castor: Levallois implementation days at contract rate; internal PD charged at the ESM standard rate. Total €8.4 m.

fields.what: Known unavailability of critical resources: unavailable from / to plus the reason.
fields.castor: Marie Curie unavailable during the EFSF bond rollover overlapping the parallel run.

fields.what: Whether a resource is fully assigned to the project or shared, with a percentage and a comment.
fields.castor: Grace Hopper 50%, retaining her Senior Loan Operations Officer duties; Nikola Tesla 100%.

fields.what: The resource buffer, in time or units, held against identified uncertainties or risks.
fields.castor: Buffer on architect days against R-07, the loss of Levallois's key architect.

fields.f: Project Schedule — Start Date / End Date
fields.what: Start and end date per breakdown component, derived from dependencies and effort, giving the overall project duration.
fields.castor: Release 1 ends 26 Mar 2027; Release 2 ends 17 Dec 2027; parallel run 08 Jan – 30 Apr 2028; go-live 15 May 2028.

fields.what: Milestone list, bar chart, Gantt chart, network diagram or linked bar chart — often several, chosen for project size and control needs.
fields.castor: Milestone schedule for the PSC plus a Gantt chart for the Project Core Team.

fields.what: Names the Handbook and every other plan whose activities are costed and scheduled here, so nothing is planned twice or not at all.
fields.castor: Handbook, Outsourcing Plan, Transition Plan and Business Implementation Plan; all their activities appear in the breakdown.

fields.what: Related documents by title, version, date and location — including previous baselines of this plan and their status reports.
fields.castor: Baseline v1.0 of 26 Jun 2026 plus the Levallois contract of 18 Sep 2026 triggering re-baseline v2.0.

traps: Accountable is the PSC — unlike the Handbook, which the PO approves.
Must cost and schedule ALL activities, including Transition and Business Implementation ones.
Three parts in fixed order: Work Breakdown → Effort & Cost Estimates → Schedule.
It elaborates Charter scope; new scope needs a Change Request, not a redraft.
Baselined and signed off, then kept current — the file always holds the latest baseline.
